title: E-Beam Inspection - Contamination Detection on Candela 8520
subtitle: Post-Clean Quality Validation for 10nm Node Manufacturing
author: James Rodriguez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Candela 8520 system to detect and classify Contamination defects during post-clean inspection at the 10nm technology node. The test is conducted at Chandler Fab 42 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Contamination defects that are critical to yield at the 10nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Candela 8520 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Candela 8520
- Inspection Type: E-Beam Inspection
- Target Defect: Contamination
- Process Step: Post-Clean
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 10nm
- Fab Location: Chandler Fab 42

This test case applies to all Candela 8520 systems deployed at Chandler Fab 42 for post-clean monitoring in the 10nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Candela 8520
Software Version: v11.8.724
Recipe: E-BEAM_INSPECTION_10nm_POST_CLEAN
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (176 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Candela 8520 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'E-Beam Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Contamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 10nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 83 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 90% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.3% for E-Beam Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.97 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-08-05
Wafers Tested: 30
Total Defects Found: 4884
Defect Density: 690.95 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.9%
Capture Rate: 87.2%
Test Duration: 356 minutes
System Uptime: 98.7%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Candela 8520 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Contamination at the 10nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
